triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix threshold selector mapped filing_status 4 (surviving spouse) as well as 1 to qualified_tips_phaseout_threshold_joint, giving a surviving-spouse return the $300,000 phaseout start that 26 USC 224(b)(2)(A) allows only 'in the case of a joint return'; the fix narrows the joint threshold to filing_status == 1.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release: 224(b)(2)(A) reads 'reduced (but not below zero) by $100 for each $1,000 by which the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income exceeds $150,000 ($300,000 in the case of a joint return)'. A surviving spouse under 26 USC 2(a) uses the joint RATE schedule but does not file a joint return, so $150,000 is right for filing_status 4. Corroboration: the sibling overtime statute in this same commit (index 40, statutes/26/225.yaml) already mapped 4 => other for the identical '$150,000 ($300,000 in the case of a joint return)' clause, so 224 was the outlier and this commit aligns them; policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/income-tax-brackets.yaml confirms 4 = surviving spouse (test case 'surviving_spouse_uses_joint_schedule'), and statutes/26/1211.yaml confirms 2 = married filing separately. Caveats for a reviewer: no commit or PR sentence names this defect (the message is generic validation-repair language), and the same module diff also (a) wraps qualified_tips_modified_adjusted_gross_income, employee tips and nonemployee tips in max(0, ...) clamps that have no basis in 224(b)(2)(B) ('the adjusted gross income of the taxpayer ... increased by any amount excluded'), (b) re-expresses taxpayer_is_married_individual_within_section_7703 as filing_status in {1,2}, (c) renames taxable_year_begins_after_december_31_2028 -> taxable_year_begins_after_termination_date, (d) adds a deferred_outputs block for subsection (d) qualified-tip classification, new 911/931/933 imports, and many local import proof atoms. The filing-status narrowing is the only change that corrects encoded meaning against the source.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix selector routed filing_status 4 to qualified_tips_phaseout_threshold_joint (300000), and the post-fix formula gives the joint threshold only to filing_status == 1, so a surviving-spouse return drops from a $300,000 to a $150,000 phaseout start — a real change in encoded meaning to a formula, not metadata. I verified filing_status 4 is surviving spouse in this repo (statutes/26/1/j.test.yaml case "surviving_spouse_uses_joint_schedule" sets filing_status 4 and expects 5504, identical to the filing_status 1 case; 26/1211.yaml pins 2 as married-separate), and the pinned corpus text for us/statute/26/224 (release us-rulespec-2026-07-13) reads only "exceeds $150,000 ($300,000 in the case of a joint return)" with no surviving-spouse extension — unlike 26 USC 1(j)(5)(B) in the same corpus, which expressly says "in the case of a joint return or surviving spouse". Refutation attempts failed: the rewrite was not compiler-forced (26/1211.yaml still uses a five-branch `match filing_status` at this same commit), the excerpt/citation churn elsewhere in the diff is separable from this formula edit, and the post-fix value is the one the cited text supports. The defect is a population/filing-status scope error, so wrong_entity_or_scope fits; untraceable_branch is the close runner-up since the fix literally deletes an ungrounded branch.
